sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Petition No.8235 Of 2019
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner/A1 to quash the proceedings against him in CC.No.4507 of 2019 on the file of XVII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad at Nampally.

entities.text: XVII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad at Nampally
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Section 420 r/w.34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.
3.
The grievance of the 2nd respondent/defacto complainant is that an agreement of sale with GPA was executed on 03.12.2005 vide document No.4254/2005 in the office of Sub-Registrar.
Though his name is mentioned at Serial No.7 as Vendor, he was not present in India and his signature and thumb impression were forged.

He approached this petitioner herein and two others who are the vendees not to act in any manner by virtue of the document No.4254/2005, however the petitioner acted in the way prejudicial to the interests of the complainant.
4. On the basis of the said complaint, the Police investigated the case and filed charge sheet under Section 420 r/w.34 of the Indian Penal Code.
5. Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that it is a registered document and it was not used in any manner in order to cause loss to the defacto complainant.
As such, the question of attracting offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code does not arise.

6. On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor would submit that it is stated in the charge sheet and the statement of the victim that though he pleaded with this petitioner and two others regarding the document being executed, the petitioner did not pay any attention to him and caused loss to him.
For the said reason, it amounts to an offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
7. The disputed document is a registered document.
The name of the 2nd respondent is sown at serial No.7 as 'represented by GPA Ali Bin Awad, s/o. late Sultan Awad Bin Omer.

The said GPA holder had gone to the registration office on behalf of the 2nd respondent and registered the document in favour of this petitioner and two others, along with seven other vendors.
8.

In the said circumstances, when the 2nd respondent was represented by GPA holder while registering the document, the grievance if any should be against the family members of the GPA Buddaram Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118127939/
1 holder and cannot prosecute the petitioner for the offence of cheating.
9.

entities.text: GPA Buddaram Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To attract an offence of cheating the essential ingredient is an act of deception played by the person pursuant to which the person deceived should have delivered property.
10. Even according to the 2nd respondent, he did not know about this petitioner until 2015 when he came back to Hyderabad.
The question of this petitioner either misrepresenting or deceiving the 2nd respondent in any manner does not arise.
If the person acting as GPA holder is not empowered, the petitioner herein can proceed against him.
11. The offence is one of forgery and cheating.
Even according to the charge sheet, the offence of forgery was not made out.
When the offence of forgery is not made out, the question of cheating does not arise.

12. Accordingly, the petitioner succeeds and the Criminal Petition is allowed quashing the proceedings against the petitioner in CC.No.4507 of 2019 on the file of XVII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad at Nampally.
